axes.label: Low setup
axes.help: How little you prepare before it runs.

axes.label: Low quota
axes.help: How little of your token quota it burns.

axes.label: Autonomy
axes.help: How long it runs without you.

axes.label: Low re-read
axes.help: How little of the spend goes to re-reading the same context.

axes.label: Stays on track
axes.help: How unlikely it is to drift off course without you noticing.

axes.label: Understanding
axes.help: How much you understand of the result at the end.

scale: 0-3, higher is better on every axis. Ordinal judgement from the sources. Numbers under Low quota and Low re-read come from one run on sonnet (roman-numeral task, bench/README.md): one run, an anecdote, not a ranking.

pick.label: Pick one per task
pick.help: Each one answers 'how do I attack this?'. The stateful loop has two variants: whether each round re-reads the session or starts clean.

addon.label: Add to another
addon.help: They do not attack the task on their own: they change where a form runs, who gives advice, or how work continues tomorrow.

between.label: Between tasks
between.help: Not for one task: it makes the next one start better.

forms.name: Conversation
forms.one: Turn by turn: you judge every answer.
forms.when: There is no check a command can run (design, writing, decisions), or the task is small.
forms.con: You have to be there; the agent's 'done' is not verified on its own.

forms.name: /goal + goal contract
forms.one: A small model reads the conversation after every turn and decides whether the goal is met.
forms.when: A one-sitting task whose end a command can prove.
forms.pro: Zero setup; a fresh judge decides when it is done; works with claude -p.
forms.con: The judge runs no commands, it only reads what was shown; one goal per session; context keeps growing.

forms.name: Stop-hook gate
forms.one: When a turn ends a command runs; if it fails, the agent keeps going with the error as its next instruction.
forms.when: A repo where 'done' is always the same command (mvn test, npm run build).
forms.pro: Deterministic judge, no tokens; applies to every session in the repo.
forms.con: It has to be installed; a slow check delays every turn that changed something.

forms.name: Subagents (orchestrator-worker)
forms.one: The orchestrator splits the work, each worker solves one piece in its own context, and the orchestrator verifies.
forms.when: Useful parallel work, context isolation, or a bounded independent review; piece count alone is not a reason.
forms.pro: The main context stays clean; each worker can be isolated in a worktree.
forms.con: Each worker re-reads its own share; the orchestrator carries the plan turn by turn.

forms.name: Dynamic workflow
forms.one: The graph as a script: a splitter cuts the work, workers run in parallel, plain code merges, a gate closes.
forms.when: Repeated independent work where explicit coordination and merging improve coverage or throughput enough to justify setup.
forms.pro: The plan is code you can read and rerun; cross-verification; resumes what already finished.
forms.con: The most expensive form; no human input mid-run; small plans cap how many agents it can start.

forms.name: Stateful loop - in session
forms.one: The same session takes one item per round from a short state file, does it, verifies it and logs the evidence elsewhere.
forms.when: A project of many items, each with a technical VERIFY, while you stay around.
forms.pro: Moves item by item on its own; the state survives a /clear.
forms.con: Every round re-reads the whole session context: the form that burns the most quota.

forms.name: Stateful loop - fresh session
forms.one: A script outside the agent relaunches it with the same prompt, a fresh session per round, state kept in files.
forms.when: Hours with nobody around, with long waits that do not need the agent (builds, GPU jobs).
forms.pro: Fresh session per round: no context re-read; stops on round cap, on no progress or on a STOP file.
forms.con: The script has to be written and tested; startup hooks are chosen by hand.

e:
next round - or stop: cap,
no progress, STOP file

forms.name: Background sessions (agent view)
forms.one: Several background sessions, each in its own worktree with its own /goal; you see which one needs input.
forms.when: Two or three independent tasks while you leave or do something else.
forms.pro: Survives closing the terminal; one /goal per session; isolated from each other.
forms.con: Each session spends like a full session; research preview.

forms.name: Advisor
forms.one: A cheap model does the work and an expensive one weighs in only at the moments that matter.
forms.when: Serial work that is hard only in spots: many turns between a few real decisions, and a smaller model stalls only on those.
forms.pro: The strong model is paid only when consulted, so its cost scales with how often the worker gets stuck.
forms.con: Helps only if the worker actually consults it; in Anthropic's own test it cost about 2.1x the worker alone for a gain at the edge of noise, and it cannot add capability the worker lacks. Beta tool; recheck each model release.

forms.name: Cloud routine
forms.one: A cloud agent runs on a schedule or a GitHub event and leaves a PR or a note.
forms.when: Something periodic on a GitHub repo that does not need your machine.
forms.con: Cannot see local files; hourly at most; runs without asking for permissions.

forms.name: Context reset + handoff
forms.one: You end the session and the next one starts clean with a handoff written for its goal, instead of compacting.
forms.when: Long sessions, or work that continues tomorrow.
forms.pro: The new session drags no old context; the handoff is short and points at one goal.
forms.con: The handoff has to be written before cutting; it is not a session summary.

e:
next goal, decisions,
open items, files

forms.name: Learning inbox
forms.one: A pass re-reads past sessions and proposes memory or skill changes to an inbox you approve.
forms.when: Weekly, or every few long sessions.
forms.pro: What was learned reaches the next run without anyone having to remember it.
forms.con: Without human approval, noise gets into memory.

principles.name: Context rot
principles.one: More tokens in context, worse recall of what is right in front of the model. Attention is a finite budget.
principles.rule: keep state files and always-loaded memory short.

principles.name: Retry cap
principles.one: With a noisy judge, more repair rounds can break what was already right. Stop and report.
principles.rule: two failed VERIFYs mark the item BLOCKED; three tries per unit in workflows.

principles.name: Progressive disclosure
principles.one: Load only what the current step needs and leave the rest behind a name and a description.
principles.rule: a memory index instead of the memories, skills loaded by description, the wiki index first.

principles.name: Context discipline
principles.one: The cost is the context you send, not the task you ask for: search before reading whole files.
principles.rule: grep with context before opening a file; summarize and drop.

principles.name: Generator-evaluator
principles.one: Whoever writes does not grade itself: an evaluator with a different context reviews evidence, not impressions.
principles.rule: the orchestrator runs VERIFY; a separate verifier before shipping.

principles.name: Over-constraint
principles.one: Too many rules, or rules that contradict across layers, make the model worse. One place per instruction.
principles.rule: a lean CLAUDE.md; judgement over rules except in critical zones.

principles.name: Blast-radius gate
principles.one: Supervision depends on how hard the action is to undo, not on how confident the model is.
principles.rule: deny the irreversible, ask on the last step; ask before side effects outside the repo.

n:
Ask focused questions
or inspect evidence

Are you staying
at the computer?

Long sequential work,
or parallel tasks?
decision_tree.note: A starting point, not an automatic choice: keep direct work as an alternative when setup outweighs the benefit. Without an automated check, delegated review stays bounded, not autonomous. If work continues tomorrow, add a context reset + handoff.
